sectors.name: Technology
themes: Global AI capex and memory-chip supercycle (Hynix, Samsung) is the primary demand driver, lifting Indonesian tech via supply-chain and sentiment linkages, not local fundamentals.
Indonesia's digital economy—e-commerce, fintech, and data-center buildout—remains underpenetrated, offering structural growth for local tech names despite global volatility.
Rupiah stability and BI's rate trajectory are key swing factors: a dovish pivot would re-rate high-beta tech, while a hawkish hold caps multiples.
sectors.ai: Buy Indonesian tech selectively: global AI/semiconductor strength (SK Hynix +30%, Samsung +27%) is spilling into local names, but the +1.85% ID move is broad, not deep. Favor liquid large-caps with earnings visibility (MLPT, IRSX) over speculative PMUI/MSKY. Trim into strength if IDX tech hits 2% daily gain; re-enter on pullbacks to 200-day moving averages.

US-China trade fragmentation and EV battery supply diversification accelerate Indonesian nickel's strategic premium, insulating INCO from US equity weakness and underpinning long-term capex cycles.
sectors.ai: Buy selective nickel and tin names (INCO, TINS) on the IDX strength; ALKA/FPNI spikes are speculative, take profits. The sector's US lag is noise—Indonesia's downstream processing and export ban leverage remain the core edge. Accumulate AGII for coal-to-gas transition exposure, but avoid chasing BAJA/RMKO without volume confirmation.

Formal retail channel expansion in tier-2/3 cities is accelerating, benefiting mid-cap staples UNIC and GZCO over the next 12 months.
sectors.ai: Buy consumer staples selectively on IDX strength: IATA, SGRO, and AGAR show momentum from rural demand and palm-oil-linked FMCG input leverage. Rotate out of US-exposed names (INDR, BACH) as IDR strength and domestic consumption hold. Target UNIC and OPMS for defensive yield; trim GZCO on valuation risk.
